concepts.def: X- ion with full outer shell

walkthroughs.body_html:
2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2.

Test gas with a lit splint - squeaky pop.

Solution turns indicator purple (alkaline).

2Na + Cl2 -> 2NaCl.

Sodium loses e- (oxidised), chlorine gains e- (reduced).

Product is an ionic salt.

Cl2 + 2KBr -> 2KCl + Br2.

Chlorine is more reactive than bromine.

No reaction if added halogen is less reactive (e.g. I2 + KCl).

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
